questions.stem: Copper pyrites is an ore of copper that contains copper, iron and sulfur.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The percentage composition by mass of copper pyrites is Cu 34.60% Fe 30.52% S 34.88% Show, by calculation, that the empirical formula of copper pyrites is $ \mathrm{C u F e S_{2}} $

parts.label: b
parts.text: Copper is obtained from copper pyrites in a two-stage process. Stage 1 Copper pyrites is heated in air. $2 \mathrm {C u F e S} _ {2} + 3 \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {C u S} + 2 \mathrm {F e O} + 2 \mathrm {S O} _ {2}$ Stage 2 The copper(II) sulfide is separated and then heated in air. It reacts with oxygen to form copper and sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State why the sulfur in the reaction in stage 1 is described as being oxidised.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the reaction that occurs in stage 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Sulfur dioxide dissolves in water to form an acidic solution.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Identify the ion that causes this solution to be acidic.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State how litmus paper can be used to show that the solution is acidic.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Give two observations that are made when a piece of magnesium ribbon is added to the acidic solution.

parts.label: b-i

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Using information from the table, state the relationship between the reactivity of a metal and the temperature rise.

parts.label: b-iii

questions.stem: A mixture of carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and hydrogen is known in industry as synthesis gas. Synthesis gas is converted to methanol, $ \mathrm{C H_{3} O H} $ , by passing it over a heated solid catalyst. The equations for the two reactions are $\begin{array}{l l l l} \mathrm {R e a c t i o n 1} & \mathrm {C O (g)} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {C H} _ {3} \mathrm {O H} (\mathrm {g}) & \Delta H = - 9 1 \mathrm {k J / m o l} \\ \mathrm {R e a c t i o n 2} & \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) + 3 \mathrm {H} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {C H} _ {3} \mathrm {O H} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {g}) & \Delta H = - 4 9 \mathrm {k J / m o l} \end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text: Assume that both reactions reach a position of equilibrium.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: For reaction 1, predict whether using a high or a low temperature would produce the higher yield of methanol. Give a reason for your choice. prediction reason ...

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: For reaction 2, predict whether using a high or a low pressure would produce the higher yield of methanol. Give a reason for your choice. prediction reason ...

parts.label: b
parts.text: The catalyst increases the rate of both the forward reaction and the backward reaction. Suggest why the catalyst has no effect on the position of equilibrium.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Reaction 1 can be represented by a reaction profile diagram.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Complete the profile by showing the products of the reaction and the enthalpy change, $ \Delta H $ , for the reaction.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Draw an arrow on the profile to represent the activation energy for the forward reaction. Label this arrow E.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: State the effect, if any, of the catalyst on the enthalpy change for the reaction.

questions.stem: The mineral rozenite contains crystals of hydrated iron(II) sulfate, $ \mathrm{F e S O_{4}. x H_{2} O} $ She uses this apparatus to remove and collect the water of crystallisation from a sample of iron(II) sulfate crystals. She uses this method. weigh empty tube A to find its mass place a sample of hydrated iron(II) sulfate crystals into tube A and reweigh heat tube A allow tube A to cool and reweigh repeat the process until the mass no longer changes Heating until the mass no longer changes is known as heating to constant mass. When iron(II) sulfate crystals are heated gently, they decompose according to this equation. $\mathrm {F e S O} _ {4}. x \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {F e S O} _ {4} + x \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ These are the student's results. A student wants to find the value of x.

parts.label: c
